app_store_whats_new:
MQTT settings can find the root topics in use near you. The search button on the Root Topic field listens to your broker for a minute and lists your region, state and city topics with the nodes heard on each, plus the other active topics nearby. Picking one fills in the field; nothing is sent to the radio until you save. It also checks a typed topic against the firmware's rules. The Root Topic field now accepts the firmware's full 31 characters instead of 30.

Node cards in the Nodes list show the node's hardware model, such as Heltec V4, once the node has announced it.

Radiation readings (microroentgen per hour) from a node's environment sensor now show in Environment Metrics, with their own filter and chart, on the dashboard Environment widget, on World Mesh node cards and in the environment CSV export. A node with only a radiation sensor now records history too.

Fixes:
- Usage analytics and crash reporting now stay off from the moment the app first starts until you choose to share them. On a fresh install they were briefly on before the app switched them off, and crashes recorded while crash reporting was off could be sent later if you turned it on. Those are now deleted instead.
- Crash reports you choose to share no longer include your saved radio's Bluetooth identifier, profile text from a failed profile save, or email addresses, phone numbers and keys found in error messages and the steps leading up to a crash.
- Buying a pack you already own no longer opens the payment options. The App Store or Google Play and Stripe were offered side by side even when the pack was already unlocked through the other one, or through the Complete Pack, so it could be paid for twice. The app now says you already own it and charges nothing.
- Resend now works on a direct message that only a relay node acknowledged. Tapping it used to do nothing visible: the message went out again, but its bubble kept showing the relay's tick. It now shows the new attempt and its outcome. A message the recipient has already confirmed is never sent again.
- After you disconnect from a MeshCore radio over Bluetooth, the Devices screen lists it as MeshCore straight away. It briefly showed a Meshtastic badge until the scan found the radio, and tapping it in that moment tried a Meshtastic connection.
- While the Devices screen is still searching, it says it is looking for Meshtastic and MeshCore radios when MeshCore support is on, instead of Meshtastic devices only.
- Connecting to a radio, or an MQTT feed, that reports thousands of nodes no longer freezes the app. NodeDex linked every recently heard node to every other, copying each node's links per pair, so a node database of 20,000 froze the app for minutes while its memory climbed; it now links the 64 most recently heard nodes in each window and keeps each node's 256 strongest links. Node names from a large node database are also saved in batches rather than one full rewrite per node. A first connect to a 20,000-node radio now finishes in about 15 seconds.
- Counts of 1,000 or more show a thousands separator in your language, such as Nodes (20,004).
